# Results — Study 248 (Presidential-Honeymoon) on real data

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The presidential-honeymoon
claim: the S&P 500 earns excess returns in the first 100 calendar days after each
inauguration. Ticker: **^GSPC** (price index, no dividends — fine for the *relative*
comparison against the next 265 days). As-of **2026-06-15**.
25 inaugurations from Hoover (1929) through Trump's second term (2025).*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | n days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| ^GSPC | 1928-01-03 → 2026-06-15 | 24,729 | `cc8b1977fb03` |

## Per-inauguration 100-day honeymoon vs next-265-day control

Each inauguration gets two raw returns: the first 100 calendar days (honeymoon) and the
next 265 calendar days (control period).  The comparison is within-term, so it is immune
to trend changes across decades.

| President | Year | Honeymoon ret | Control ret | HM wins? |
|---|--:|--:|--:|:---:|
| Hoover | 1929 | -1.5% | -8.1% | yes |
| FDR | 1933 | +78.3% | +6.3% | yes |
| FDR (2nd) | 1937 | -9.3% | -28.4% | yes |
| FDR (3rd) | 1941 | -10.3% | -5.1% | no |
| FDR (4th) | 1945 | +9.4% | +24.5% | no |
| Truman | 1949 | -4.7% | +14.7% | no |

**Honeymoon wins: 11 / 25 terms (44%)**

## Headline test: honeymoon minus control, paired

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| n inaugurations | 25 |
| Honeymoon mean (100 cal days) | **+3.29%** |
| Control mean (next 265 cal days) | **+4.64%** |
| Paired difference (HM − Control) | **−1.34 pp** |
| **HAC t-stat (diff)** | **−0.29** |
| Positive-rate (HM > Control) | **44%** |

The paired diff t-stat is **−0.29** — not only below the |t| ≥ 2 bar, but negative.
The honeymoon *underperforms* the control period on average, by −1.34 pp.

## First-year vs second-year extended test

A broader window: does the first calendar year after inauguration outperform year two?

| n terms | Year-1 mean | Year-2 mean | Diff | HAC t |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 25 | +8.57% | +4.72% | +3.85 pp | +0.65 |

The diff t-stat of +0.65 suggests no reliable first-year advantage either — the
positive mean difference is consistent with pure noise.

## Post-2001 subsample (7 inaugurations)

In modern data (post-2001, 7 terms), the honeymoon *clearly underperforms*:

| Metric | Full history | Post-2001 |
|---|--:|--:|
| HM mean | +3.29% | +1.42% |
| Control mean | +4.64% | +14.06% |
| Diff (HM − Control) | −1.34 pp | **−12.64 pp** |
| HAC t (diff) | −0.29 | **−3.83** |

The modern subsample actively contradicts the honeymoon narrative: the 100-day window
after recent inaugurations has been *considerably worse* than the subsequent months.

## Structural honesty note: why even +78% does not save the claim

FDR's 1933 honeymoon (+78.3%) is a 100-day outlier driven by the New Deal's emergency
bank-closure measures and Depression-era recovery — not a 'honeymoon effect'. Excluding
it, the full-history diff becomes more negative. The claim requires a systematic
excess return across terms; what we see is noise plus one extreme outlier.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Paired HAC t-stat = −0.29; n = 25; honeymoon underperforms control
  on average. No subsample shows a positive significant differential; post-2001 shows
  significant *underperformance* (t = −3.83 in the other direction). Stamp: None.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** A honeymoon-only buy rule earns +3.29% raw over 100 days
  versus +4.64% in the control window; even before costs, the edge is negative.
  Opportunity cost (75% of the year in cash) makes it worse. Stamp: Mirage.
- **Beats a coin? — BUSTED.** 44% of terms show HM > control, which is below a fair
  coin. The folk belief of a market honeymoon is statistically unsupported and directionally
  wrong in modern data.
